title: Renaming a receiver must move its map entry, not just overwrite in place
answers: After renaming a receiver, the old one still shows up (ghost/duplicate receiver)
How does UpdateReceiver handle a name change?
Rename leaves stale entry in AMConfigV1.Receivers
body: Invariant: a receiver's map key (`v1.ReceiverUID(name)`) is derived from its mutable name field, so renaming a receiver changes which key it must live under. Enforced in `ConfigRevision.setReceiver` (legacy_storage/receivers.go): it inserts the new receiver under `ReceiverUID` of the *new* name, then explicitly `delete`s the old UID key when `persistedRecv.UID != receiver.UID`. If skipped, UpdateReceiver leaves a stale entry under the old key alongside the new one — a duplicate/ghost receiver in the stored config. Constraints: applies to any future create/update path for receivers, and to any other resource whose map key is derived from a mutable field — must move the entry, not just overwrite the value at the old key.
says: After renaming a receiver, the old name still appears in list.
Why does the renamed receiver show alongside the original name?
Receiver rename creates a duplicate ghost entry in configuration.
How is receiver name change handled in the system?
Old receiver entry doesn't disappear after renaming to new name.
search: A receiver's map key in pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/receivers.go is derived from its mutable name field via v1.ReceiverUID(name), so renaming requires moving the entry to a new key, not just overwriting. ConfigRevision.setReceiver enforces this by inserting the new receiver under the new ReceiverUID and explicitly deleting the old UID key when persistedRecv.UID != receiver.UID; skipping the delete leaves a stale ghost receiver under the old key. This invariant applies to UpdateReceiver and any future create/update path for receivers, and to any resource whose map key derives from a mutable field—always move the entry, never just overwrite the old key.
